newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy official says everyone should retire at 65.
newsitem.headline: Italy official says everyone should retire at 65.

text.p: Italians should in future all be expected to retire at the age of 65 and pensions should only be granted earlier in special cases, Italy's state auditor Andrea Monorchio said on Thursday.

Monorchio told a parliamentary commission that so-called seniority pensions, which can be drawn after 40 years of contributions have been paid by an employee into a state retirement fund, should be phased out.
Monorchio said this type of pension was "a privilege which already in a lot of countries does not exist."
Anyone seeking to draw a pension before the age of 65 should be penalised. "An actuarial calculation should be applied to reduce the pension to the point of being no longer desirable," he said.
The benefit to state coffers from the lower recourse to early retirement could be valued in the order of "thousands of billions" of lire, Monorchio added.
